threat_cases.evidence: Both lookup request schemas require exact keys and classify any caller-supplied root, payload, status, digest or approval field as lookup_request_schema_invalid.

The lookup caller has no snapshot or authority field. Expected authority and verified bytes enter only through canonical_improvement_binding_owner_boundary_v1; replacing lookup request bytes cannot replace that owner-controlled dependency.
Snapshot identity, digest, owner, sequence, epoch, predecessor digest and external root are compared with the independently read authority and produce invalid_snapshot on drift.
The expected authority pins snapshot bytes, publication sequence and epoch. The synthetic rollback pair is rejected with snapshot_authority_binding_mismatch.
Genesis is restricted to sequence/epoch 1/1 and null predecessor fields; linked snapshots require the immediately prior sequence, an earlier epoch and a full predecessor digest.
A snapshot or entry effective after as_of returns not_effective. A future entry can be bound into forensic result evidence but cannot become found or a semantic adapter value.
The project strict explicit-instant parser rejects unsupported timestamps; lookup returns not_effective with lookup_as_of_not_explicit_instant.
Instants are canonicalized from epoch nanoseconds to UTC with exactly nine fractional digits. Offset-equivalent inputs produce byte-identical lookup results.
Duplicate entry identities and typed lookup keys, including conflicting bytes, invalidate the complete snapshot without deduplication.
Reuse of a bound identity across previous_binding and capture_binding is classified as snapshot_cross_type_identity_collision.
Entry type and source namespace inventories are closed and versioned; unknown types and namespace/type mismatches invalidate the snapshot.

The store exposes only lookup_previous_binding and lookup_capture_binding. Compatibility adapters expose only the three predecessor lookup methods; static scans found no mutation, filesystem, provider or database path.
The observed digest is returned only from a found store result and AJ/AC/AQ classify a mismatch against their independently derived expected digest as an explicit semantic collision.
Capture identity and observed snapshot/entry digests remain bound; matching and conflicting capture observations produce distinct downstream evidence.
Snapshot, entry and observed binding digests are part of each result digest. Distinct collision bytes therefore produce distinct forensic store and downstream result identities.
AJ, AC and AQ receive only the exact read adapters. Their existing canonical verifiers rebuild lookup observations; no caller status or trust boolean is accepted.
Both gates return before the owner dependency getter. Instrumented counters remain zero for request, snapshot, clone, authority, entry, digest and downstream work.
Store, harness and lookup results bind literal shadow-only, no-live, no-automatic-change, no-promotion, no-external-AI-authority and synthetic/not-publishable metadata.
Golden JSON is fixture-only, performance_claimed:false and publishable:false; documentation explicitly forbids real Ture performance interpretation.
The implementation imports server-only. Repository and build scans found no app, component, page, route, provider, database, writer or persistence consumer.
